Its history includes the World War II landing in Lingayen Gulf and a strong civic and cultural landscape around the provincial Capitol complex. Its coastal setting, the Agno River, and an 11.5-kilometer coastline support fisheries and other aquatic resources, while local tourism highlights heritage buildings, the Baywalk, and the Limahong Channel. Best for  Heritage: Casa Real, the Capitol complex, Sison Auditorium, churches, and WWII memorial sites.  Coastal leisure: Lingayen Beach and Baywalk, sunsets, walks, and photo stops.  Food tourism: Lingayen bagoong, bagoong-based dishes, sundot-kulangot, kalamay, and local seafood.  Ecotourism: Limahong Channel, its tourism center, and the nearby bike/ecotourism area."}

The present city was created from the former municipality of San Carlos under Republic Act No. 4487 in 1965. The Province of Pangasinan describes San Carlos as a major trading center for bamboo and a leading producer of carabao mangoes. The city government presents San Carlos as an agro-industrial, commercial, educational, and tourism center. Its tourism character is centered on heritage, agriculture, mangoes, bamboo crafts, food, parks, and inland resorts."}

The city tourism site says it is held annually around the last Saturday of April and promotes the city's mangoes and bamboo products while recognizing farmers and producers. Festival activities have included float parades, street dancing, mango culinary contests, bamboo-craft competitions, variety shows, and Laro ng Lahi. Exact dates and activities can change each year, so check the City Government's announcements before traveling. San Carlos City also became known for a giant mango pie made for the 2011 festival. The city tourism site records the event as a 100-square-meter mango pie prepared using about 2,000 kilograms of ripe mangoes and shared after public viewing."}

Its strategic location has made it a major trading and agricultural hub. The provincial government identifies rice, vegetables, and noodles among products associated with the city, while the City Government highlights its markets, rice fields, cultural spaces, parks, and resorts as visitor experiences. Unlike Pangasinan's coastal destinations, Urdaneta's tourism character is centered on city life, agriculture, food, culture, faith, commerce, and inland leisure."}
